lab_title: AR Heart Anatomy and Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major blood vessels of the human heart.
Trace the path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
Explain the structural differences between the left and right ventricles based on their function.
Describe the role of the heart valves in ensuring unidirectional blood flow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: To introduce the heart's external structures and its position within the thoracic cavity.
key_visuals: A life-sized, anatomically correct 3D model of the human heart.
Major vessels such as the aorta, pulmonary trunk, and vena cavae are clearly visible.
A semi-transparent outline of the rib cage and lungs to provide anatomical context.
student_actions: Manipulate (rotate, scale) the heart model to view it from all angles.
Identify and select the major vessels entering and leaving the superior aspect of the heart.

scenes.brief_purpose: To identify the four chambers of the heart and understand their basic arrangement.
key_visuals: The heart model with a coronal cross-section, revealing the internal chambers.
Sequential highlighting of the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
Clear labels for each chamber appear upon selection.
student_actions: Tap on each of the four highlighted chambers to correctly identify them.

scenes.brief_purpose: To locate the four heart valves and understand which chambers and vessels they separate.
key_visuals: A close-up view of the heart's interior.
Highlighting of the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid), and aortic valves.
Simple animations showing the valve leaflets opening and closing.
student_actions: Select each valve to learn its name and anatomical location.
Match each valve to the two structures it separates (e.g., Mitral valve separates the left atrium and left ventricle).

scenes.brief_purpose: To trace the path of deoxygenated blood from the body through the right side of the heart to the lungs.
key_visuals: An animated flow of blue particles representing deoxygenated blood.

The path of blood is shown entering the right atrium via the vena cavae, passing through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle, and being ejected through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary artery.
student_actions: Initiate the animation for the pulmonary circuit.
Tap on structures in the correct sequence as the deoxygenated blood flows through them.

scenes.brief_purpose: To trace the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs through the left side of the heart to the rest of the body.
key_visuals: An animated flow of red particles representing oxygenated blood.
The path of blood is shown entering the left atrium via the pulmonary veins, passing through the mitral valve to the left ventricle, and being ejected through the aortic valve into the aorta.
student_actions: Trigger the animation for the systemic circuit.
Identify the key structures involved in the pathway of oxygenated blood.

scenes.brief_purpose: To understand the functional reason for the difference in myocardial thickness between the left and right ventricles.
key_visuals: A transverse cross-section of the ventricles, emphasizing the muscular walls (myocardium).
The myocardium of the left ventricle is visibly thicker than that of the right.
Visual indicators (e.g., pressure gauges or animated arrows) showing the relative force of contraction for each ventricle.
student_actions: Answer a question explaining why the left ventricle's wall is thicker, relating it to the higher pressure needed for systemic circulation versus pulmonary circulation.

scenes.brief_purpose: To synthesize all previous steps into a single, dynamic visualization of the full cardiac cycle.
key_visuals: The full heart model with both red and blue blood particles flowing simultaneously and continuously.
The four valves are animated, opening and closing in coordination with the flow of blood, demonstrating systole and diastole.
The dual-loop nature of circulation is clearly visualized as blood flows to the lungs and body concurrently.
student_actions: Observe the complete, synchronized blood flow.
Control the speed of the animation to better understand the timing of valve action and chamber contraction.
